notes: Day 1 climbs about 900 m to Okaka Lodge. It is a long day: start early.
A local trust operates the lodges. Book them with the track operator, not with DOC.
The tops are open to wind and cold. Wet boardwalk is slippery.

portcraigschool.name: Port Craig School Hut
portcraigschool.note: DOC hut. You must book before you go. Facilities: heating, mattresses, non-flush toilets. Boil the water before you drink it.

okakalodge.name: Okaka Lodge
okakalodge.note: Lodge of the Hump Ridge Track near the top of the ridge, with bunk rooms and a kitchen. You must book with the track operator.

portcraiglodge.name: Port Craig Lodge
portcraiglodge.note: Lodge at the old sawmill town of Port Craig. You must book with the track operator. The DOC Port Craig School Hut is next to it.

start.name: Rarakau car park
start.note: Start and end of the circuit, 20 km west of Tuatapere.

pois.name: Percy Burn Viaduct
pois.text: One of the largest wooden viaducts in the world that still stands: 125 m long and 36 m high. It carried the timber tramway of the Port Craig sawmill in the 1920s.

pois.name: Edwin Burn Viaduct
pois.text: Wooden viaduct of the Port Craig timber tramway. The track crosses it.

pois.name: Hump Ridge tops
pois.text: The highest part of the track, about 920 m. A loop walk above Okaka Lodge goes between sandstone tors and small lakes.

pois.name: Ōkaka Lodge
